challenges.title: First Contact
challenges.summary: Read the welcome letter waiting in your home folder.
hints: Use `ls` to list the files in the folder where you are.
Use `cat <file>` to print the content of a file.

challenges.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
challenges.summary: Your access badge is in your home folder... but `ls` does not show it.
hints: On Linux, files whose names start with a dot (.) are hidden.

challenges.title: Station Map
challenges.summary: Find the main configuration file of the station and read its onboarding code.
hints: Linux keeps configuration files in one specific top-level folder. Check 'Folder Structure' in the CheatSheets.
Go to /etc with `cd /etc` and look for a folder named after the company.
Inside that folder, `ls` and then `cat` the file that looks like the station configuration.

challenges.title: The Captain's Log
challenges.summary: The captain left a PRIVATE note somewhere inside a very long log file.
hints: Logs usually live under /var/log. Look for the station's folder there.
The file has thousands of lines. Open it with `less <file>`, type `/PRIVATE` and press Enter to search.
Inside less: `n` jumps to the next match, `q` quits.

challenges.title: Not What It Seems
challenges.summary: In ~/cargo one file is lying about what it is. Find it and read it.
hints: An extension (.jpg, .pdf...) is just part of the name. The `file` command looks at the real content.
Go into the cargo folder and run `file *` to inspect every file at once.
Look for the file that `file` reports as text even though its name says otherwise.

challenges.title: Tidy Up the Deck
challenges.summary: Follow the orders in ~/deck/README_FIRST.txt and pass the inspection with `inspect-deck`.
hints: `mkdir -p a/b/c` creates nested folders in one go.
Wildcards save time: `mv *.log logs/` moves every file ending in .log.
`cp` copies (the original stays), `mv` moves (the original disappears), `rm` deletes.
